To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) water at low relative humidities binds to open metal sites in a metal-organic-framework and forms disconnected one-dimensional hydrogen-bonded chains bridging between coblat atoms; (ii) with increasing relative humidity these water chains nucleated pore filling, with water occupying the entire pore interior at 30% RH; (iii) the properties of pore confined water are significantly different than bulk water, and water molecules display variable mobility as a result.

the hydrogen bonding structure of confined supercritical water in a metal-organic-framework (MOF) is significantly different from bulk liquid water, and that this difference is due to the formation of a one-dimensional chain of hydrogen bonded water molecules that bridges between open metal sites in the MOF.

water confined in a metal-organic-framework with open metal sites forms one-dimensional chains that nucleate pore filling at low relative humidity, and that the mobility of water molecules is variable as a function of the distance from the interface.
